author: NorthEast News Desk
body: An explosion struck a weapons-storage site near Tsareva Livada in central Bulgaria overnight, starting a fire that spread from one warehouse to another. Authorities reported no injuries in the initial accounting. The incident is the second at a Bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks, adding urgency to the investigation while firefighters and security officials assess the site.

Bulgarian media identified the facility as being operated by EMCO, an arms-trading company associated with businessman Emilian Gebrev. The cause of the latest blast had not been established in the early reports. That uncertainty is significant because Bulgaria has previously investigated a series of explosions at facilities storing ammunition intended for Ukraine and Georgia.

In 2024, Bulgarian authorities issued warrants for six Russian nationals accused in older depot explosions between 2011 and 2020 and linked those cases to an attempted poisoning. Moscow denied the allegations. There was no announced evidence connecting the Tsareva Livada blast to those cases, and the current fire remains a developing event. The immediate verified facts are the explosion, the warehouse-to-warehouse spread and the absence of reported injuries.
dek: No injuries were reported after an overnight blast near Tsareva Livada, the second incident at a Bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks.
headline: Explosion and fire spread through Bulgarian weapons depot
